issues.description: Concrete animal class names differ between the problem/template and the solution. The problem statement UML and the template Main refer to concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (students are instructed to implement/ use Seal, Pig, Goat). The solution repository instead provides concrete implementations named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat and leaves Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java empty. This mismatch breaks the name-to-concept mapping the exercise relies on: code in the template (Main) and the UML expect Seal/Pig/Goat, but the working implementations in the solution are only available under the Space* names, which will confuse students and can cause compilation or integration issues when code references the expected class names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the concrete class names consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat in the solution to Seal, Pig, Goat (preserving their implementations and constructors), or (B) add concrete Seal, Pig, and Goat classes to the solution that extend or delegate to the corresponding Space* classes so that Seal/Pig/Goat exist with the expected constructors and behaviors. Ensure the class names used in the problem statement, template Main, and solution match exactly so students and automated tests use the same identifiers.
